doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Recording sessions with the Hampton band
summary: Recordings were relaxed because the band already knew the tunes, mostly popular tunes of the day.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Okay. When you went to do records with the Hampton group, was it a lot of time pressure to get in so many songs in one session?

Well no, not really. Because these were tunes that we’d been playing. Most of the time it was tunes — then we’d have about three or four tunes in there that some of the guys wrote or some other composer wrote that we would install in there. But generally it would be tunes that, well from the popular tunes of the day you know, or let’s say of the era.
And most of the recording didn’t take that long, it didn’t take that long if I can remember.
